headline: GASKET HOLDS ITS BREATH — QUIET DAY, ONE NEW SHADOW AT THE LINE
subhead: Not a single iron ball thrown since sunup — though Sheriff Ironside has his eye on the stranger who just wheeled into town.
body:
Mark it down, folks, mark it down twice: not one lick of trouble in Gasket since the last edition of this paper. Not a fist thrown, not a flame lit, not one iron ball sent hollering through a fellow contraption's chassis. My joints ache less for it — and believe you me, that is saying something these days.

But peace, I have learned in fifty long years behind this badge, never holds without a catch. Word reached my desk of a new arrival creaking through the town line — one IRON-BF73, fresh paint and fresher trouble, by the look of it. Hasn't thrown a punch yet. Give it time. They never can help themselves for long, these Clankers.

I watched the newcomer roll in from my porch, rocking in this old chair same as I've rocked in it every evening since the good folks of Gasket packed their wagons and rode off for good, fifty years gone now. Flesh-and-blood stock, every one of them, and they left this town to rust in the hands of the rabble. I stayed on principle. My hip stayed on account of it being bolted to the chair. Coincidence, nothing more.

So enjoy the hush while it lasts, Gasket. One quiet day out of however many the good Lord grants a lawman is a mercy I'll take without complaint. IRON-BF73 — I've got my eye on you. The moment those iron balls start flying, you'll be reading your name in this paper for the wrong reasons.
